Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline’s records permit direct payments to every affected member, so a claims process is unnecessary. We propose a $32 million class fund with automatic distribution. Fees would be paid separately, subject to court approval, and any amount not awarded would go to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that direct, automatic payments are appropriate. To move toward a settlement that delivers meaningful relief without further litigation, Brightline proposes a $27 million class fund and $3 million in fees, subject to court approval. Any fees not awarded would go to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. Those terms provide a strong basis for settlement. To close the remaining gap on class relief, we propose a $30 million class fund while accepting your proposed $3 million fee amount, subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement on the fee amount and our agreement on automatic distribution. Brightline can increase the class fund to $28.5 million, with the remaining terms as proposed, to move us closer to resolution.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. To resolve the remaining $1.5 million gap, we propose splitting it: a $29.25 million class fund, with automatic payments and all other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Agreed. Brightline accepts your latest term sheet, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with an automatic-distribution settlement that delivers substantial value to the class. Keep fees separate, subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class rather than Brightline.

The $35.5 million proposal is within authority and has court-friendly terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total cash outlay. Counter with automatic distribution and no fee reversion to preserve approval prospects.

The $27 million fund with automatic payments is a serious offer, particularly given certification and trial risks. There is room to seek a modest improvement without compromising direct relief or introducing fee terms that disadvantage the class. Keep fees at defense counsel’s proposed level and direct any unawarded amount to the class.

The latest offer is within authorization and has strong approval prospects, but there is room to reduce Brightline’s outlay while preserving automatic payments and straightforward fee terms. Counter at $28.5 million for the class, with fees unchanged.

Brightline’s $28.5 million automatic-distribution fund is a strong offer given trial and certification risks. A modest counter at the midpoint could improve class recovery without disturbing the agreed protective terms.

The $32.25 million total is within authorization. Automatic distribution and the absence of clear sailing or a fee reversion to Brightline support court approval. The modest potential savings from another counteroffer do not justify risking this agreement.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this declaration in support of preliminary approval. The parties reached a binding settlement, subject to court approval, providing a $29,250,000 class fund and automatic payments to identified class members without a claims process. Brightline will separately pay up to $3,000,000 in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any amount not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. I do not disclose confidential mediation communications. Fees were discussed before agreement on class relief; I therefore do not represent that fee discussions occurred only afterward. Hargrove Lane LLP’s compensation is fixed at $3,500,000 regardless of the outcome, and any settlement fee award is paid to the consumer-protection foundation, not the firm. In my judgment, the settlement merits preliminary approval: it provides substantial, automatic cash relief now, while avoiding material certification and trial risks and a further estimated two to three years before trial.
